title: Restormer: Efficient Transformer for High-Resolution Image Restoration
description: Hand-labeled golden set for retrieval evaluation. Each item's gold_pages lists the PDF pages (1-based, matching the chunk page field) whose chunks contain the answer. answers are reference facts for a later faithfulness/LLM-judge eval, not the retrieval metric.

items.answer: Restormer is the 'Restoration Transformer', an efficient transformer model for high-resolution image restoration.

items.query: What is the main limitation of existing transformer models that Restormer addresses?
items.answer: Quadratic self-attention complexity and the inability to model long-range pixel interactions over high-resolution images.

items.query: How does the multi-dconv head transposed attention (MDTA) achieve linear complexity?
items.answer: It applies attention across feature channels (channel-wise self-attention) instead of the spatial dimension, avoiding quadratic cost in spatial size.

items.query: What does GDFN stand for and what is its role?
items.answer: Gated-Dconv Feed-forward Network; it gates the information flow through a feed-forward network to control the transformation.

items.query: What PSNR does Restormer achieve on CBSD68 for Gaussian color image denoising?
items.answer: Around 34.67 dB at sigma=25 (state of the art across sigma=15/25/50).

items.query: How does Restormer compare to SwinIR on Gaussian grayscale denoising?
items.answer: Restormer outperforms SwinIR by a notable PSNR margin while being more efficient.

items.query: What is the progressive training strategy used by Restormer?
items.answer: A three-stage progressive training schedule that starts with smaller image patches and crops and gradually increases patch size and reduces batch size.

items.query: What datasets are used to train Restormer?
items.answer: ImageNet, DIV2K, Flickr2K, and BSD datasets, depending on the task.

items.query: Does Restormer process full images or image patches?
items.answer: It processes the full high-resolution image (not cropped patches), thanks to the linear-complexity attention.

items.query: What are the two core modules of the Restormer transformer block?
items.answer: The multi-dconv head transposed attention (MDTA) and the gated-dconv feed-forward network (GDFN).

items.query: What is the channel-wise transposed attention design in MDTA?
items.answer: Query, key, and value are depth-wise convolution projections that aggregate spatial context, then attention is computed across channels.

items.query: What do the ablation studies show about the number of transformer blocks?
items.answer: A deep-narrow design performs more accurately than a wide-shallow counterpart, though the wider model runs faster due to parallelization.

items.query: What tasks does Restormer handle beyond denoising?
items.answer: Image deraining, deblurring, and defocus deblurring, in addition to denoising.

items.query: Does Restormer use self-attention over spatial pixels?
items.answer: No; it uses channel-wise attention (MDTA) instead of spatial self-attention, which is what keeps it linear.
items.note: Contrast to prior transformers in Section 3.
